extracted.intended_audience: Public Information Officers (PIOs), emergency management communicators, and PIO trainees
extracted.subtask_description: Training/guidance for Public Information Officers on their roles, functions, required knowledge, skills, and operational practices during incidents and steady-state. Covers JIS/JIC, ICS/NIMS familiarity, media relations, target audiences, rumor control, tools, and whole-community awareness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency management knowledge (must know)
rubrics_metrics.description: The PIO must know basic emergency management concepts, Incident Command System (ICS), and the National Incident Management System (NIMS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understanding these systems enables the PIO to operate effectively across local, tribal, state and federal levels and to know how their organization fits into the overall response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Familiarity with local Emergency Operations Plan (should understand)
rubrics_metrics.description: The PIO should be familiar with the local Emergency Operations Plan and his or her organization’s role in an emergency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Knowing the EOP and organizational responsibilities helps the PIO advise leadership and coordinate information consistent with operational roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding of ICS
rubrics_metrics.description: ICS is a standardized, on-scene, all-hazard approach to incident management used across organizations and levels of government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PIOs should know when ICS is used (all incidents and planned events), its benefits (clarifies chain of command, interoperable communications, planning processes), and that ICS provides a common framework for integrating resources and personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding of NIMS
rubrics_metrics.description: NIMS provides a systematic, proactive approach to guide departments and agencies at all levels to work seamlessly across prevention, protection, response, recovery, and mitigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Familiarity with NIMS helps ensure coordinated information and public affairs across jurisdictions and sectors to reduce loss of life and property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint Information System (JIS) purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: JIS integrates incident information and public affairs into a unified organization that provides consistent, coordinated, accurate, accessible, timely and complete information to the public and stakeholders during incident operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: JIS operates across and supports ICS, EOC, and MAC Group; PIOs should use JIS principles when developing and delivering public information.

rubrics_metrics.name: JIS activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Developing and delivering coordinated interagency messages; developing, recommending and executing public information plans and strategies; advising on public affairs issues that could affect incident management; addressing and managing rumors and inaccurate information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These activities are performed in support of Incident Commander/Unified Command, EOC Director, and MAC Group and should be coordinated among public information personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint Information Center (JIC) role
rubrics_metrics.description: The JIC is a central location that houses JIS operations where public information staff perform essential information and public affairs functions; normally a single JIC is preferred though multiple may be accommodated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PIOs should understand the JIC as the hub for information coordination and staffing during an incident.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advising leadership on public information matters
rubrics_metrics.description: PIOs must advise the Incident Commander, Unified Command or EOC director on public information matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advisory role includes assessing public information implications and recommending messaging, briefings, interviews, and media engagement strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gathering, verifying, coordinating, and disseminating information
rubrics_metrics.description: PIO functions include gathering, verifying, coordinating, and disseminating accurate, accessible, and timely information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the ongoing information cycle: gather complete information, verify accuracy, coordinate with other JIS personnel for consistency, then disseminate consistent, coordinated, accurate, accessible, timely and complete information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling inquiries
rubrics_metrics.description: Handle inquiries from the media, public and elected officials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond promptly and professionally; returning calls and answering emails builds credibility and trust with media and stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Providing emergency public information and warnings
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide emergency public information and warnings as part of PIO duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely, clear warnings can be life‑saving; ensure messages are accessible and reach targeted audiences quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rumor monitoring and response
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct rumor monitoring and response to address and manage inaccurate information that could undermine public confidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proactively identify misinformation and correct it through coordinated JIS messaging to maintain public trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information cycle (gather-verify-coordinate-disseminate)
rubrics_metrics.description: An ongoing information cycle: Gathering complete information; Verifying information to ensure accuracy; Coordinating information with other public information personnel; Disseminating consistent, coordinated, accurate, accessible, timely and complete information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this four-step cycle systematically during incidents to ensure message quality and consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: ICS Functional Areas and Command Staff awareness
rubrics_metrics.description: Every incident requires certain functional areas to be implemented (identify problem, assess, develop/implement plan, procure resources); PIOs should understand ICS management structure and how they receive assignments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Knowing the structure and functional needs helps PIOs interact with Command Staff and integrate public information into incident objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incident Commander role awareness
rubrics_metrics.description: The Incident Commander is responsible for the overall management of the incident and is the only position always staffed in ICS applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PIOs should know how to advise and support the Incident Commander or Unified Command and recognize command authority and transfer procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytical (quality of an effective PIO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyze what’s going on and make strategic decisions to operate proactively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analytical PIOs assess the environment, public perception, and operational information to shape messaging and outreach (example: develop strategies to build community understanding during budget crises).

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic (quality of an effective PIO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Make strategic decisions and develop plans that advance the organization’s goals through public information activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Link messaging to broader organizational objectives and look for opportunities to shape public understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proactive (quality of an effective PIO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Operate in a proactive manner—anticipate issues and act before they escalate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proactive actions include arranging interviews, partnerships, or public engagement to build support and understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledgeable / Credible (quality of an effective PIO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Can speak with authority and credibility on all facets of the organization’s operations; knows where the organization fits in the bigger picture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Being knowledgeable builds trust; credibility is reinforced by delivering what is promised and responding reliably to media and stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assertive (quality of an effective PIO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Effectively navigate dynamic situations to seek out important information and provide solid, thoughtful advice to leadership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assertiveness helps redirect negative questions and ensure important information is surfaced and communicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trusted (quality of an effective PIO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Has proven to be reliable and trusted by both media and organization; returns calls and answers e-mails from the media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trust is earned through consistency, accuracy, and timely follow-through.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexible (quality of an effective PIO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Can adjust plans and priorities as the situation requires.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flexibility allows PIOs to adapt messaging and tactics when incidents evolve or new information emerges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Able to perform under pressure (quality of an effective PIO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Can meet demands of the situation without losing composure or sacrificing good decision making; has good public-speaking skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain clear communication and manage stress to ensure consistent messaging during high-pressure incidents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessible (quality of an effective PIO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Be accessible to the news media; accessibility is critical because other qualities won’t matter if the PIO isn’t reachable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide reliable contact methods, respond promptly, and maintain open lines of communication with media and stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional professional dispositions (objective, advocate, educator)
rubrics_metrics.description: Be objective; be an advocate for the public, organization, and media; be an educator to help new reporters and build relationships during steady-state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balancing objectivity with advocacy and education strengthens public information efforts and media relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify external target audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: External audiences include the general public and the news media that act as a conduit to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and tailor messages to these audiences to ensure effective reach and comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify internal target audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Internal audiences include organizational leadership, communications advisors, and the workforce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep internal stakeholders informed about what is being told to media and what media is reporting so they can relay accurate information to the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal communications alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Tell internal audiences what you are telling the media, and also let them know what the media is saying.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This enables uniform messaging from uniformed personnel and first responders, who are often public-facing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whole community awareness
rubrics_metrics.description: Know the community demographics, governmental structure, key players (people and organizations), relevant history, and community culture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The whole community approach ensures solutions that serve the entire community and leverages resources from government, non-governmental, and private-sector organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media relations — provide information and access
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop credibility and build relationships with the media by consistently providing information and access to newsmakers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer timely access to officials and subject matter experts to meet media needs and foster trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media relations — understand media needs and operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate an understanding of media needs and operations (e.g., reporters stay until they get the information they need).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate media deadlines and workflows to better serve their needs and get accurate coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media relations — respect media deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Respect media deadlines as a core part of media relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely responsiveness increases the likelihood of accurate reporting and favorable coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media relations — maintain open dialogue and engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain open dialogue with the media; consider regular meetings (quarterly or otherwise) to allow questions and feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Routine engagement (quarterly meetings, state-level coordination) strengthens relationships and preparedness before incidents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing for the public (style and channel adaptation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Writing for the public is different than writing reports; adapt style to the delivery channel and use the Associated Press Stylebook.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Well-written products assist media (may be used as-is) and direct attention to the most important information when deadlines are tight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of sound bites
rubrics_metrics.description: When speaking to the media, think in terms of sound bites — short, catchy statements often quoted or replayed by the media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare concise, quotable lines that communicate key messages clearly under deadline pressure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparedness: tools and resources (Go Kit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Have readily available tools: office supplies; laptop/tablet/smartphone and portable printer with alternate power sources; maps; broadcast recording equipment; extra cell phone batteries; fax; agency letterhead; camera; battery-powered radio; pre-scripted messages and template releases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain a prepared Go Kit and keep it updated as part of steady-state planning so materials are available during incidents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-established vendor/partner agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish agreements with businesses/agencies prior to an incident for translation services, printing companies, and communications companies to assist operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracts enable rapid access to translation, printing, and communications installation (WiFi/cell/hard-line) when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure accessibility of messaging
rubrics_metrics.description: Disseminated information must be accessible to the public and stakeholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider language access, disability access, and multiple channels to reach diverse community members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness, accuracy, coordination, and completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Information must be timely, accurate, coordinated among partners, and complete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure in any of these dimensions can undermine public confidence and incident response; use JIS coordination to maintain these standards.
